question: Can day-5 and day-7 functional measurements forecast the day-12 network-spike readout for unseen chemicals in a held-out culture-date group?
target_definition: log2 of the arithmetic mean across replicate wells of (ns.n + 1)/(same-plate same-DIV zero-dose median ns.n + 1)
identities: Experimental-summary CAS or named NOCAS identifier; explicit author-supported aliases; resolve repeats before splitting
reserve_rule: The latest three experiment-date groups, selected using metadata before model fitting. Purge every reserved chemical identity from development. Do not score the reserve in this selection sprint.
development_split: Leave one remaining experiment-date group out; additionally purge every test chemical identity from training, including repetitions on other dates.
features: Only days 5 and 7: arcsinh(mean raw readout), arcsinh(mean same-plate control median), missing fraction per readout; plus log10 concentration and the two target-readout normalized values. No identities, plate/date IDs, future measurements, viability, published potency, toxicity, or full-trajectory annotations enter models.
primary_metric: Within each held-out date, average absolute log2 error over doses for each chemical, then over chemicals; average these date losses equally.
secondary_metrics: per-date paired comparison against the strongest baseline
uncertainty: 10000 paired resamples of development experiment-date losses; descriptive bootstrap, not a confirmatory independent-study confidence claim.
selection_interpretation: Assess the gain over persistence, strong target-only learners, and full-feature Ridge; consistency over culture dates; error on large late changes; and feasibility of a useful workflow. No universal 15% or 20% competition cutoff is asserted. Do not claim saved experimental days, toxicity, recovery after washout, or living-chip validation from this retrospective forecast.
